name: SDN Host HTTP Request Node
description: Capability node wrapping the host http.request hostcall. Method "request": input "request" JSON {"method":"GET|POST|...","url":"https://...","headers":{...},"bodyB64":"<base64 request body>","timeoutMs":N} -> one "response" frame of UTF-8 JSON bytes {"status":N,"headers":{...},"bodyB64":"<base64 response body>"}. The node decodes bodyB64 and forwards the raw bytes as the hostcall binary segment; the request meta carries both host dialects (timeout_ms/timeoutMs, body_encoding=base64, responseType=binary) so one payload serves every host. Response handling is host-agnostic: the SDK NodeHost/BrowserHost return the body as raw bytes (binary segment; response limited only by host policy), while the Go server host (sdn-server modulert/caps/http.go) returns body as a JSON string with body_encoding utf8|base64 and caps the response body at 4 MiB — the node normalizes both to bodyB64. Capability "http" is required on all hosts.

externalInterfaces.description: Outbound HTTP through the host http.request hostcall. Go server host: 4 MiB response cap, 30 s default timeout. SDK NodeHost/BrowserHost: fetch-based, origin allowlists enforced by host policy.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON bytes (aligned-binary wire format): {"method":"GET","url":"https://..." (required),"headers":{"Name":"Value"},"bodyB64":"<base64>","timeoutMs":30000}. Only url is required; method defaults to GET.

inputPorts.description: The HTTP request descriptions. THIS IS A FAN-IN PORT: the compiled flow runtime does not enforce maxStreams or maxBatch when it fills an invocation (space_data_module_runtime_begin_node_invocation pops the node's whole queue up to the drain budget), so an upstream node that fans out N descriptors delivers all N here in ONE invocation. The method drains every frame and emits one response per request, in input order. It was declared maxStreams 1 while the entry read only frame 0, and the N-1 frames the runtime had already dequeued were destroyed silently — live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider, where a two-provider request performed exactly one outbound fetch.

acceptedTypeSets.description: UTF-8 JSON bytes (aligned-binary wire format): {"status":<HTTP status>,"headers":{...verbatim from the host...},"bodyB64":"<base64 response body>"}. bodyB64 is always base64 regardless of which host dialect returned the body.

outputPorts.description: The HTTP responses: EXACTLY ONE frame per request frame consumed, pushed in input order, so response k answers request k. A request that could not be performed still emits its frame, carrying status 0 plus "error"/"errorMessage" and an empty bodyB64 — status 0 is outside 2xx so a consumer that filters on status drops it exactly as it would drop a 500, while the slot stays aligned. Emitting nothing for a failure is what previously shifted every later body one slot left and let a consumer attribute a payload to a provider that never served it.

methods.description: Performs one outbound HTTP request per input frame through the host http.request hostcall and emits the normalized responses in input order. Fetches within an invocation are SEQUENTIAL — the hostcall is synchronous — so a batch costs the sum of its members' latencies plus whatever the host's own per-destination egress pacing adds. A frame that fails is skipped and the batch continues; a non-zero status is returned only when no request in the batch succeeded.
